method: Historical melody staff read separately from the content generator. Original-pitch and rhythm tokens are retained here, with explicit transposition, form, and ornament choices. This file must never be regenerated by build-songbook.py. Source review covers melodies; original harmony, implementation, and physical listening are separate checks.

long-long-ago.part: Vocal staff, one verse, excluding piano introduction and postlude
long-long-ago.findings: Initial draft had incorrect durations, omitted rests, and incorrect pitches. Corrected to the historical vocal line. Original accompaniment is checked separately in harmony-review.json.

fur-elise.edition: Breitkopf & Härtel 1888, public-domain transcription by Stelios Samelis (Mutopia 931)
fur-elise.part: Opening right-hand eight-bar period, pickup and first ending, one pass; no left-hand or later sections
fur-elise.findings: Corrected incorrect dotted durations and regrouped notes/rests into original measures. Theme scope is explicitly labeled; no claim of the complete bagatelle.

sweet-afton.part: Vocal melody, once; omit small ornament at dis-, omit terminal quarter rest; piano introduction and postlude excluded
sweet-afton.findings: Replacement for unresolved Water Is Wide version. First-edition image read directly. Fermatas remain discretionary, not an automatic tempo change.

home-sweet-home.edition: McKinley Music Co., circa 1914, vocal setting of Bishop’s 1823 melody
home-sweet-home.part: Vocal staff only, verse and refrain once; no piano introduction/postlude
home-sweet-home.findings: Vocal score inspected across all three pages; pitches cross-checked against separate Gutenberg MIDI Synth Voice track. MIDI has expressive timing and is not the duration oracle. Initial draft was incorrect and replaced. Source edition dating corrected; original 1823 composition provenance still needs final rights documentation.

home-on-range.edition: Cowboy Songs and Other Frontier Ballads (1910), Gutenberg notation transcription
home-on-range.part: Vocal staff, verse and refrain once; tied durations combined into a single sounding event
home-on-range.findings: Replaced incorrect draft rhythm and form. Three-page vocal score inspected; 74 source attacks corroborated against separate Gutenberg Voice MIDI track. Expressive MIDI gate lengths were not copied. Distinct historical six-eight version is declared.

brahms-lullaby.edition: Brahms Op.49 No.4, voice/piano edition held by Indiana University; public-domain Mutopia 1037 transcription by Shogo Mori (2007)
brahms-lullaby.part: Complete vocal melody once, omit introductory rests and small grace notes, trim terminal rest; no piano part copied
brahms-lullaby.findings: Read melody LilyPond independently. Corrected missing rests, dotted rhythms, and second-half octave errors in initial draft. Contemporary SATB arrangement not used.

minuet-g.edition: Bach-Gesellschaft, public-domain Mutopia 75 transcription by Allen Garvin
minuet-g.part: Upper voice, all 32 bars, each section once; grace notes and mordents omitted
minuet-g.findings: Read relative-octave source independently; second section reaches B5 in source (B4 sounding on guitar). Bar 8 corrected to dotted-half A, omitting optional grace B.

greensleeves.edition: Grove, A Dictionary of Music and Musicians, vol.1 (1879), Greensleeves; tune from William Chappell, Popular Music of the Olden Time (1859)
greensleeves.part: Complete historical monophonic tune, both sections once; no lyrics or existing harmony copied
greensleeves.findings: Corrected second-section rhythm and high C-sharp in source (F-sharp in guitar key), internal cadence and final repeated attacks. This is the declared historical variant, not a modern recording arrangement.

frere-jacques.edition: Vieilles chansons pour les petits enfants (1883), Gutenberg transcription, first vocal entry only
frere-jacques.part: One complete traditional round melody. Rebarred to begin on beat one; later contrapuntal entries and Widor accompaniment excluded.
frere-jacques.findings: Read first voice across both source pages. Original starts with a two-quarter pickup; own guitar arrangement shifts the bar grid by two quarters, preserving all 32 quarters and every melody event.

twinkle.edition: Vieilles chansons pour les petits enfants (1883), Ah! vous dirai-je, maman, vocal staff
twinkle.part: Complete traditional tune, 24 source 2/4 bars paired into 12 guitar 4/4 bars; no accompaniment copied
twinkle.findings: This historical French variant has E-E-E-D at the two middle cadences. Draft used a different modern familiar cadence; corrected and exact variant declared.

mary-lamb.edition: Carmina Collegensia, expanded edition (1876), supplement p.55, Mary Had a Little Lamb (Hobart Version)
mary-lamb.part: Upper melody, first complete verse only; following verse and medley excluded; separate pickup before fleece joined to preceding bar
mary-lamb.findings: Corrected familiar tune attribution (not the different Lowell Mason melody), repeated B notes in bar 4 and dotted rhythms. Added final eighth rest in place of the next verse pickup to close the standalone instrumental phrase.

auld-lang-syne.edition: The Popular Songs of Scotland, J. Muir Wood, Edinburgh, 1887, pp.240–241
auld-lang-syne.part: One verse and chorus, no introduction or piano copied; terminal rest trimmed
auld-lang-syne.findings: Read vocal staff across both pages, magnifying Scotch snaps. Corrected high F pickup, repeated-note rhythm, chorus entry snaps and final cadence. Guitar note values doubled (2/4 to 4/4) for beginner counting; pitches transposed F to G and lowered register.

drink-to-me.edition: Anonymous late-eighteenth-century melody, Carr Baltimore glee (Levy 038/040); Cambridge critical transcription N.2.1/1 used for legible pitch comparison
drink-to-me.part: Treble 1 complete tune; initial four-bar strain repeated with both endings, followed by remaining eight bars. Tied same-pitch cadences merged into one attack. No other voices copied.
drink-to-me.findings: Approved-list replacement for unresolved Saints. Melody traced to eighteenth-century glee rather than a modern song arrangement. Critical edition records uncertain authorship; app credits Traditional, not an asserted composer.

ash-grove.edition: Edward Jones, The Bardic Museum (London, 1802), p.83, Llwyn-onn
ash-grove.part: Complete 24-bar principal tune, each section once, excluding following six-eight variation and lower voice. Small grace and turn ornaments omitted.
ash-grove.findings: Directly inspected the 1802 score. Replaced incomplete and incorrect 16-bar draft with the complete principal tune. Historical variant includes developed middle section; it is not a transcription of a twentieth-century arrangement.

oh-susanna.edition: Oh! Susanna, 1848 engraved edition, vocal staff pp.2–4. Complete 16-bar verse and 8-bar chorus with pickup; piano material excluded. Original C-major guitar accompaniment.
oh-susanna.part: Complete instrumental melody, one pass; historical accompaniment and lyrics excluded
oh-susanna.findings: Read each vocal line directly from the historical score. Corrected incomplete verse, chorus pitches and durations, sixteenth-note pickups, and final rest. No lyrics or other choral voices copied.

blue-bells.edition: The Blue Bell of Scotland, G. Willig, Philadelphia, circa 1800–1801, Levy 031/034. Early vocal version: first strain twice, second strain once; introduction/postlude and small ornaments excluded. New guitar harmony.
blue-bells.part: Complete instrumental melody, one pass; historical accompaniment and lyrics excluded
blue-bells.findings: The previously cited 1803 Scottish Musical Museum tune was a different version. Replaced draft with the identifiable early Willig melody. Slurred identical pitches merged into held tones; no trill/grace expansion; final quarter rest omitted.

london-bridge.edition: Singing Games, Josephine Pollard (1890), p.100. Complete familiar eight-bar tune in its historical cadence variant. Note values doubled into 4/4; original guitar accompaniment.
london-bridge.part: Complete instrumental melody, one pass; historical accompaniment and lyrics excluded
london-bridge.findings: Directly inspected the 1890 printed staff. Replaced secondary Rosewig reference with this accessible primary score. Preserves its final two-bar variant and eighth rest. No illustrations, lyrics, game text, or existing accompaniment copied.

row-your-boat.edition: Franklin Square Song Collection (1881), p.69, E. O. Lyte round. One complete voice; historical 6/8 version with repeated third-degree notes in bar 3. Original guitar harmony.
row-your-boat.part: Complete instrumental melody, one pass; historical accompaniment and lyrics excluded
row-your-boat.findings: Directly inspected original printed p.69 (PDF page 74). All eight bars, the repeated third-degree notes in bar 3, and held final notes match the independently entered reference. Round performed as one voice only; no historical harmony copied.

amazing-grace.edition: New Britain, The Southern Harmony (1847 edition), p.8, tenor melody. Historical fourteen-bar setting with pickup, one pass using the final ending. New G-major guitar harmony; no hymn text included.
amazing-grace.part: Complete instrumental melody, one pass; historical accompaniment and lyrics excluded
amazing-grace.findings: Read tenor shape-note staff in the original scan, corroborated by Bethel NewBritain MIDI onsets. Corrected modernized/invented phrase lengths, passing notes and duplicate final attack. Repeated second section omitted; final ending retained.

ode-to-joy.edition: Beethoven’s joy theme (1824), complete sixteen-bar melody as printed in The Hymnal (Presbyterian Board, 1911), no.115. Original C-major guitar setting; Amen and hymn accompaniment excluded.
ode-to-joy.part: Complete instrumental melody, one pass; historical accompaniment and lyrics excluded
ode-to-joy.findings: Compared directly with the historical 1911 score image, upper voice only. Retains that edition’s two eighth notes near the final cadence. This is the familiar hymn-form theme, not the complete symphonic movement.

rejectedReferences.reason: Different melody; cannot substantiate the familiar Merrily We Roll Along tune.
Different melody; not Ah vous dirai-je maman.
Different 6/8 tune; does not substantiate the familiar 4/4 melody.
PDF identifies circa 1914 edition despite host book date; underlying melody can be compared, but this is not evidence of an 1823 edition.
